plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero for capital preservation.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and cutting underperforming names. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL, SPAL, and MUU to reduce overall leveraged ETF exposure.
Sell SMCI and SNOW due to being below stop or flagged sell.

balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while blending broad index and quality tech. Expect moderate drawdowns and steady growth potential.

plan: Add to SOXL, SPAL, and MUU to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Sell SMCI and SNOW as they are below stop or flagged sell, adhering to discipline.
Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.

This plan uses a smaller cash buffer and wider but strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and higher concentration, which significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can incur substantial losses quickly without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Sell SMCI and SNOW to reduce high-beta single names.
Add to QQQI to 30% to increase income-generating exposure.
Add to SPY to 20% for broad index stability.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index for steady monthly distributions. While prioritizing low drawdown, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is cash-like income, not a savings account.
